title: Aida:
title_short: Aida · We Make Peace With Enemies
headline: You do not need to agree on everything to work together. Peace is made with enemies, not friends.
story: Aida is an Iranian-French activist who works with Israeli, Palestinian and other civil societies. Her lesson from four years of this work: you do not need to agree on everything to work together. Divided, people lose their power to move decision-makers.

Then she turns to the people in the room: they take immense risk just to sit together, and they are all hurt. It is not about liking each other. She ends with a call for action, now, together. Strong and hopeful.

transcript:
Auto-transcript of FX6_LVH_6355.MXF (Aida, Brussels, 15 Sep 2026). Times are mm:ss in the source file. Speaker labels are often wrong: 01:58 and 03:08 are Aida, not the interviewer.
[00:04] Interviewer: Ida, could you tell us about your work in Iran, France, and the most significant lesson you've learned?
[00:10] Yes. So I am an Iranian-French activist.
[00:14] I am the co-founder of We Are Iranian Students Association that works for the defense of Iranian students' rights.
[00:23] And I also work with Les Guerriers de la Paix in Paris that work with Israeli, Palestinian,
[00:31] but also the broader civil societies in different continents that work together towards peace, justice, and dignity.
[00:40] I think the most important lesson that I've learned those past four years is that you do not need to agree on everything to work together.
[00:55] Which has been something that is a groundbreaking, honestly, lesson given the binary narrative
[01:06] and the camps that we see in the polarization of our civil societies.
[01:12] The thing is that the more we are divided, the less we have power to put pressure on the decision-makers
[01:22] for them to take the concrete and necessary actions for the peace to prevail instead of destruction and chaos.
[01:31] And the more we are divided, the more we are distracted by our inner conflicts,
[01:37] the less we have power to actually put pressure on the people who benefit from our division,
[01:45] benefit from the conflicts, benefit from the armed industries.
[01:50] And this is the best way they have found to just weaken the power of civil societies
[01:58] who actually share exactly the same interests just regardless of where they live.
[02:07] The Iranian civil society, Palestinian, Israeli, Lebanese, French, American.
[02:14] You can take any civil society in the world, they are made of human beings who just want a dignified life
[02:21] and want to offer future generations something else than conflict, chaos, and death.
[02:27] So when we have those same, those shared interests, this is the ground to begin to work together
[02:38] without demanding that we agree on everything. We will not agree on everything.
[02:44] And we will not have justice. The world has not built itself through justice.
[02:51] The world has built itself through conflict and power balances that many, or I think all of them,
[03:02] all of those battles of powers ended up somewhere unjust.
[03:08] How we manage this as human beings and human societies is accountability.
[03:16] And this creates environments that are more or less, as much as we can, fair for people, not just.
[03:26] Justice would be giving back what people have lost, which is not possible.
[03:32] But creating an atmosphere in the future that can be more fair for a future generation,
[03:39] this is something that depends on accountability.
[03:42] So we need the civil society to be aware that they do not need to agree on everything to work together.
[03:48] So this collective power becomes something that we can use to put pressure then on decision makers.
[03:55] And they have their responsibility as well, because people who are here, they are taking immense risk
[04:02] appearing together, talking to each other. They are fighting against their intimate trauma.
[04:12] And they are all hurt. And they have so many reasons not to be here.
[04:17] And when they go back home, they have to face their community. They have to face their own inner disagreement.
[04:27] And they do all of this because they believe and they are building the ground for future decisions to be made.
[04:35] And if those decisions do not come, they will have done all those efforts for nothing.
[04:41] So it's the responsibility of decision makers also not just to upload them and be inspired by them,
[04:49] but also give them the means to have an agency to make this piece possible.
[04:55] It's not about liking each other. It's not about agreeing on everything with each other.
[05:04] We make peace with enemies. We don't make peace with friends.
[05:07] They have all understood this. And they know that they are working on this common future for common interests.
[05:17] And they need decision makers to honor this effort.
[05:21] Interviewer: I'm going to ask one last quick question because I want you to have two minutes.
[05:26] Interviewer: Could you maybe give us an example of something that has worked in Iran, maybe about the role of students or women, something specific to your work?
[05:44]-[09:12] (her answer about Iran: not used in this video)
[09:12] this dichotomy between civil society and decision makers is not working anymore.
[09:17] So we need action now and we need to do it collectively.
